title: Near-Optimal Sample Complexity Bounds for Constrained Average-Reward MDPs
claim: Hard instances can be built by attaching slow-mixing components to the leaves of a routing tree, assembled from a simple primitive.
layout: 2 panels, left tree and right primitive gadget, red/blue color coding links them
description: The figure has two panels on a white background. The left panel shows a black binary-style routing tree. The root splits into two children, which split further, with unequal branching, into several leaves. At each leaf, two short stems hang down: a red one angled diagonally and a blue one vertical. Each stem ends in a small dot. These mark the slow components embedded at the leaves. The right panel shows the primitive component. A large black node labeled x sits at the top. Curved black arrows run both ways between x and a red node z, and between x and a blue node y. Red and blue self-loop ellipses sit at z and y. The red and blue colors match across the two panels. The eye goes first to the tree, then to the colored gadget.
caption: Left: a hard weakly communicating CAMDP obtained by embedding slow components at the leaves of a routing tree. Right: a primitive component used in the construction.
abstract: Recent advances have significantly improved our understanding of the sample complexity of learning in average-reward Markov decision processes (AMDPs) under the generative model. However, much less is known about the constrained average-reward MDP (CAMDP), where policies must satisfy long-run average constraints. In this work, we address this gap by studying the sample complexity of learning an $Îµ$-optimal policy in CAMDPs under a generative model. We propose a model-based algorithm that operates under two settings: (i) relaxed feasibility, which allows small constraint violations, and (ii) strict feasibility, where the output policy satisfies the constraint. We show that our algorithm achieves sample complexities of $\tilde{O}\left(\frac{S A (B+H)}{ Îµ^2}\right)$ and $\tilde{O} \left(\frac{S A (B+H)}{Îµ^2 Î¶^2} \right)$ under the relaxed and strict feasibility settings, respectively. Here, $Î¶$ is the Slater constant indicating the size of the feasible region, $H$ is the span bound of the bias function, and $B$ is the transient time bound. Moreover, a matching lower bound of $\tildeÎ©\left(\frac{S A (B+H)}{ Îµ^2Î¶^2}\right)$ for the strict feasibility case is established, thus providing the first minimax-optimal bounds for CAMDPs. Our results close the theoretical gap in understanding the complexity of constrained average-reward MDPs.
